title: SlidingGeneralizedSmooth.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F=f+h over a convex set Q. The function f is convex and continuously differentiable on the whole ambient space. The supporting-subgradient inequalities at every point of Q imply that h is convex on Q. A minimizer exists; strong convexity is not required.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The objective separates a differentiable generalized-smooth term f and a potentially nonsmooth term h accessed through bounded subgradients.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A gradient query at any x returns exactly ∇f(x), for every call index and oracle seed. No function values are supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SlidingGeneralizedSmooth.lean: Query.gradient and the first conjunct of spec.admissible.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Additional queries return a valid supporting subgradient of h at u∈Q with norm at most M, or an exact metric projection onto Q. Subgradient selections may vary with call index and seed but always satisfy the stated inequalities. Gradient, subgradient, and projection queries each count as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SlidingGeneralizedSmooth.lean: Query.subgradient, Query.project, and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Whenever ‖∇f(x+θ(y−x))‖≤B for all θ∈[0,1], the gradient satisfies ‖∇f(x)−∇f(y)‖≤(L0+L1 B)‖x−y‖. Here L0>0 and L1≥0; global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient is not assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SlidingGeneralizedSmooth.lean: spec.valid and the segment-gradient condition in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary real Hilbert space. Public inputs include x0, L0, L1, M, R, Δ, G, and ε, with M,G≥0 and R,Δ,ε>0. Hidden instance data include f,h,Q, and ∇f. Some minimizer xstar satisfies ‖x0−xstar‖≤R, F(x0)−F(xstar)≤Δ, and ‖∇f(xstar)‖≤G. No bounded diameter of Q is assumed. Algorithms must respect a separate gradient-call cap for every seed, reply sequence, and execution prefix.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SlidingGeneralizedSmooth.lean: Public, Instance, spec.valid, the minimizer clause of spec.admissible, gradientBudget, and spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return a point x∈Q satisfying F(x)−F(xstar)≤ε for a minimizer xstar of F over Q.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε objective-gap bound hold almost surely under the joint law of the algorithm seed and oracle seeds. The total oracle budget is fixed, rather than an expected-cost bound.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SlidingGeneralizedSmooth.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law, Oracle.law, and Convergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The convex composite formulation uses gradient-dependent generalized smoothness, a public gradient bound at a constrained composite minimizer, arbitrary Hilbert-space geometry, and a separate uniform gradient-call restriction.

descriptionHtml:
Composite Generalized Smooth Minimization

We minimize F=f+h over a convex set Q in a real Hilbert space E, where f,h:E→R. The function f is convex and (L0,L1)-smooth, with L0>0 and L1≥0; h admits bounded supporting subgradients on Q. A given point x0∈Q has bounded distance and objective gap to a minimizer x⋆, where the gradient of f is bounded. Oracles return exact gradients of f, bounded subgradients of h, and exact projections onto Q. For ε>0, the goal is x¯∈Q with F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

More precisely, define F(x)=f(x)+h(x) and consider minx∈QF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, x0, and all parameters L0,L1,M,R,Δ,G,ε, whose ranges are L0,R,Δ,ε>0,L1,M,G≥0. The functions and feasible set are accessed through the three oracles described below.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and feasibility). The set Q⊆E is convex and x0∈Q. For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Generalized smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, with continuous gradient. Its (L0,L1)-smoothness means that, for every x,y∈E and B∈R, ∥∇f(x+θ(y−x))∥≤Bfor all θ∈[0,1]⟹∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤(L0+L1B)∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Solution and initial bounds). There exists x⋆∈Q such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈Q,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ,∥∇f(x⋆)∥≤G.

Assumption 4 (Oracle access). The gradient oracle returns ∇f(x) at x∈E. At each u∈Q, every reply s∈E of the subgradient oracle satisfies ∥s∥≤M,h(u)+⟨s,v−u⟩≤h(v)for every v∈Q. These conditions hold for every query history and every realization of oracle randomness. Subgradient queries outside Q carry no guarantee. At any w∈E, the projection oracle returns a point p∈Q satisfying ∥w−p∥≤∥w−u∥for every u∈Q.

Gradient, subgradient, and projection calls are counted separately. Oracle randomness may be dependent across calls, and subgradient replies may depend on the query history; the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the oracle’s randomness. After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy x¯∈Q,F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize F=f+h over convex Q in a real Hilbert space. The convex differentiable f has continuous gradient and satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤[L0+L1supz∈[x,y]∥∇f(z)∥]∥x−y∥ on the whole space. Oracles supply exact gradients, exact projections onto Q, and possibly adversarial vectors s(u) with ∥s(u)∥≤M and h(v)≥h(u)+⟨s(u),v−u⟩ for u,v∈Q. There is x⋆∈arg⁡minQF with x0∈Q, ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ, and ∥∇f(x⋆)∥≤G. Here L0,R,Δ,ε>0 and L1,M,G≥0. Target: a feasible output x with F(x)−F(x⋆)≤ε almost surely.

Total: O(AR2/ε+(1+L1R)ℓ+M2R2/ε2).

Gradients: O(AR2ε+(1+L1R)ℓ).

G is used only in the gradient-count cap.
(2) Gradient sliding (Lan 2016), Cor. 1(a), arXiv v2. Derived bound: finite-dimensional localization to X=Q∩B―(x0,2R).

Total: O(1+Ae3L1RR2ε+M2R2ε2).

Gradients: O(1+Ae3L1RR2ε).

Uses L=Ae3L1R and exact ΠX; at L1=0, use X=Q, L=L0.

 (1): gradient saving e3L1R/2 when L1R≫1 and AR2/ε≫(1+L1R)ℓ; total saving additionally requires M2R2/ε2≪AR2/ε. Only ΠQ needed. Matches leading rate for L1R≲1; scope extends global smoothness. (1): extra ℓ term at L1=0; no Bregman geometry or additional simple prox term.
(3) Normalized subgradient (Grimmer 2019), Thm. 2, arXiv v3. Derived bound, E=Rd; best iterate selected using F values.

Total and gradients: O(1+(G+M)2R2/ε2+AR2/ε+L12R2).

Includes ∇f, h′ and ΠQ calls, plus F values for selection; ΠQ is unnecessary when Q=E.

For Q=E, take G=M: matched total order unless εA≫M2 or εL1≫M; initialization can mask gains. (1): updates additionally need L0,L1,M,Δ,ε; (3) needs only R,T. Initialization term (1+L1R)ℓ exceeds L12R2 when ℓ≫L1R≥1.

Abbr: A=L0+L1G; ℓ=1+log(1+(1+L1R)Δ/(L0R2)); ΠC is exact Euclidean projection onto C; h′ denotes a returned subgradient; T is the iteration horizon in (3). Total cost counts all primitive oracle calls.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import LongTails.Template

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.SlidingGeneralizedSmooth

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

abbrev Query (p : Public) := Fin 3 × p.E

@[simp] def Query.gradient {p : Public} (x : p.E) : Query p := (0, x)
@[simp] def Query.subgradient {p : Public} (x : p.E) : Query p := (1, x)
@[simp] def Query.project {p : Public} (x : p.E) : Query p := (2, x)

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  h : p.E → ℝ
  Q : Set p.E
  grad : p.E → p.E

noncomputable def objective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (x : p.E) : ℝ := I.f x + I.h x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 3
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.M ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ q.G ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I oracle :=
    (∀ k seed x, oracle.answer k (Query.gradient x) seed = I.grad x) ∧
    (∀ k seed u, u ∈ I.Q → ‖oracle.answer k (Query.subgradient u) seed‖ ≤ q.M ∧
      ∀ v ∈ I.Q, I.h u + ⟪oracle.answer k (Query.subgradient u) seed, v - u⟫ ≤ I.h v) ∧
    (∀ k seed w, oracle.answer k (Query.project w) seed ∈ I.Q ∧
      ∀ u ∈ I.Q, ‖w - oracle.answer k (Query.project w) seed‖ ≤ ‖w - u‖) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ univ I.f ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt I.f (I.grad x) x) ∧
    Continuous I.grad ∧
    (∀ x y M, (∀ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖I.grad (x + θ • (y - x))‖ ≤ M) →
      ‖I.grad x - I.grad y‖ ≤ (q.L0 + q.L1 * M) * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    Convex ℝ I.Q ∧
    q.x0 ∈ I.Q ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.Q, IsMinOn (objective I) I.Q xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧
      objective I q.x0 - objective I xstar ≤ q.Δ ∧ ‖I.grad xstar‖ ≤ q.G)
  successful q I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.Q, IsMinOn (objective I) I.Q xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _),
        output ω ∈ I.Q ∧ objective I (output ω) - objective I xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SlidingGeneralizedSmooth
